FGEN-CTX-G3.title: Harbor & Pine customer experience team offsite - planning notes
FGEN-CTX-G3.text:
HARBOR & PINE - CUSTOMER EXPERIENCE TEAM OFFSITE
Planning notes, owner: Priya Nandakumar (updated September 29)

When and where
Thursday, November 12, 9:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
The Linden Room, Corbett Street Library Annex, 2nd floor, 118 Corbett Street.
Doors open at 9:00 a.m. for coffee. We start at 9:30 sharp.
Remote teammates can join the morning sessions by video; the link will be in the calendar invite. The afternoon planning block is in-person only.

Purpose
Agree on the team's top 3 priorities for Q1, reset how we hand off escalations between the phone and email queues, and spend some unstructured time together. This is not a performance review day.

Agenda
9:30 - Welcome and ground rules (Priya)
10:00 - Retro on Q3 and Q4: what worked, what didn't (facilitated by Tomasz Weller)
11:15 - Break
11:30 - Escalation handoff workshop (Janelle Ortiz)
12:15 - Lunch, catered by Tamarind Kitchen
1:30 - Q1 planning block (no-laptop session; bring a notebook)
3:00 - Break
3:15 - Commitments and owners
4:00 - Wrap-up and feedback
4:30 - Optional: bowling at Lucky Lanes, two blocks away (team pays for lanes; drinks are on you)

Food
Lunch is a buffet with vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options. If you have an allergy or other dietary need, fill in the dietary form linked in the invite by Thursday, November 5. After that date we cannot guarantee a separate meal. Coffee, tea and snacks are provided all day.

Budget
Total budget is $1,800, covering the room ($450), catering ($950), bowling lanes ($200) and supplies ($200). Anything outside these lines needs Priya's approval in advance.

Travel
Most of us are local. If you drive, mileage is reimbursed at 0.62 per mile through the usual expense form; submit within 30 days. The annex has a small lot that fills up by 9:00 a.m.; the city garage on Pell Street is the backup and is not reimbursed. Anyone travelling from the Westbrook office can book the 7:40 a.m. train; tickets are reimbursed.

What to bring
A notebook and pen, one example of an escalation that went badly and one that went well (anonymised), and your honest opinion.

Coverage
The support queues stay open that day. Ravi and Min-jung are covering phones and are joining by video for the morning only. Please set your status to out of office.

Questions go to Priya in the team channel.

PI-A:JD.text:
SENIOR BACKEND ENGINEER, PAYMENTS & LEDGER
Tallowmarket, Inc. | Denver, CO

ABOUT TALLOWMARKET
Tallowmarket is a B2B marketplace where independent restaurants buy directly from regional farms and ranches. Our Payments & Ledger group moves about $1.1B a year through escrowed payouts to more than 6,500 growers. We are a team of 140 people, about 55 of them in engineering. Our backend is Go on PostgreSQL, with Kafka between services and Temporal for long-running payment workflows.

WHAT YOU WILL DO
- Own services in the money path: escrow holds, split payouts to growers, refunds and chargebacks.
- Design and evolve Harrow, our double-entry ledger built on PostgreSQL, as volume grows from 400,000 to a projected 1.5 million ledger entries per day.
- Improve the reliability of the nightly settlement batch that runs at 02:00 Mountain Time and must finish before banks open.
- Lead technical design reviews and mentor mid-level engineers on the team.
- Join the on-call rotation, currently one week in six.
- Partner with Finance and Risk on reconciliation and audit requirements.

WHAT YOU BRING
- 5+ years of professional backend experience in Go, Java or Kotlin.
- Deep PostgreSQL knowledge: indexing, locking, isolation levels, and safe online migrations.
- Experience with event-driven systems (Kafka, Kinesis or similar) and idempotent processing.
- A track record of leading multi-engineer projects from design doc to launch.
- Clear written communication; we make most decisions in design docs.

NICE TO HAVE
- Prior work on a double-entry ledger or a payments platform.
- Experience reducing PCI DSS scope.
- Stripe Connect or Adyen for Platforms integration experience.
- Experience with Temporal or another durable workflow engine.

WORK ARRANGEMENT
Hybrid: in our Denver LoDo office Tuesday through Thursday; Monday and Friday are flexible. Relocation assistance is available for candidates moving to the Denver metro area.

COMPENSATION
Base salary band: $172,000 - $208,000 USD, plus equity and a 6% 401(k) match. This role is leveled at L5 (Senior).

INTERVIEW PROCESS
Recruiter screen (30 minutes), a 60-minute ledger design exercise, a Go coding session, and a values conversation with our Director of Engineering, Imani Castellanos.

Tallowmarket is an equal opportunity employer.

FGEN-CTX-G2.title: Riverbend Family Clinic - preparing for your annual physical
FGEN-CTX-G2.text:
RIVERBEND FAMILY CLINIC
Preparing for Your Annual Physical

Thank you for booking your annual physical with Riverbend Family Clinic. This sheet explains how to prepare so your visit runs smoothly. Your visit will be with Dr. Hollis Varga or a member of her care team.

Before your visit
- If your provider ordered fasting bloodwork (such as a lipid panel or fasting glucose), do not eat or drink anything except water for 10 hours before your appointment. Please avoid coffee, including black coffee, and chewing gum during the fasting period. Take your usual medications with water unless your provider has told you otherwise.
- Complete the health history questionnaire in the patient portal at least 2 days before your visit. If you cannot use the portal, arrive 30 minutes early to fill it in on paper.
- Make a list of every medication, vitamin and supplement you take, including the dose.

What to bring
- Photo ID and your current insurance card.
- Your medication list.
- Glasses or hearing aids if you use them.
- Any home blood pressure readings from the last month.

Arriving
Please arrive 15 minutes before your appointment time to check in. If you are more than 15 minutes late, we may need to reschedule you. Parking is available in Lot B behind the building; bring your ticket to the front desk for 2 hours of free validated parking. Street parking on Weller Avenue is metered.

During your visit
Your visit includes a review of your history, vital signs, a physical exam, and any screenings recommended for your age. Flu shots are available at no extra charge during your physical from October through March while supplies last. If you have a specific concern, mention it at check-in so enough time can be set aside; a separate appointment may be needed for complex issues.

After your visit
Lab results are posted to the patient portal, usually within 3 business days. Your provider will message you if anything needs follow-up. Normal results may be posted without a personal note. Follow-up visits can often be done by telehealth.

Cancellations
We ask for at least 24 hours notice if you need to cancel or reschedule. Appointments missed or cancelled with less than 24 hours notice are subject to a $40 missed-appointment fee, which is not covered by insurance.

Billing
Most insurance plans cover one preventive physical per year at no cost to you. Additional services discussed or treated during the visit, such as a new problem or a chronic condition review, may be billed separately and may involve a copay. Questions about coverage should be directed to your insurance company; our billing office can provide the procedure codes.

Front desk hours: Monday to Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.; Saturday, 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m.

FGENH-CTX-G1.title: Condo association board meeting minutes
FGENH-CTX-G1.text:
Harbor Point Condominium Association - Board Meeting Minutes
Date: Thursday, September 24
Location: Community room, Building B
Present: Linda Marsh (President), Owen Castellano (Treasurer), Priya Nair (Secretary), Hal Jensen, Beatriz Soto. Also present: Renee Okoro (property manager, Seaside Management) and 11 owners.
Quorum confirmed. Meeting called to order at 7:02 pm.

1. Approval of August minutes
Approved unanimously without changes.

2. Treasurer's report
Owen Castellano reported the operating account is on budget for the year. The reserve fund balance is $179,500. Delinquent dues stand at three units, total $4,210; the management company has sent second notices.

3. Building A elevator
The Building A elevator has been out of service intermittently since July because of a failing controller. Two quotes were received. The board voted 4-1 (Jensen opposed) to accept the Carver Lift Services quote of $38,500 to replace the controller, paid from the reserve fund. Carver estimates the work takes six to eight weeks once parts arrive; parts are on order and no arrival date has been given. Renee Okoro will post updates in the lobby and by email.

4. Roof replacement, Buildings A and B
Three bids were reviewed for full roof replacement on both buildings:
- Kessler Roofing: $212,000
- Summit Exteriors: $236,500
- Delgado & Sons: $249,000
The board voted unanimously to move forward with Kessler Roofing, subject to reference checks and a signed contract. A start date will be negotiated after the contract is signed. The treasurer noted that after the elevator payment the reserve fund cannot cover the full roof cost. A special assessment across all 64 units was discussed at length. Several owners asked for a payment plan option. The motion on a special assessment was tabled to the October 22 meeting, pending an updated reserve study. No assessment amount was agreed.

5. Pet policy
The board voted 5-0 to remove the 35-pound weight limit for dogs. The limit of two pets per unit is unchanged. All pets, including existing ones, must be registered with the management office using the new form, with proof of rabies vaccination for dogs and cats. Registration deadline: November 15.

6. Guest parking
The old paper guest passes are being retired because of misuse. Each unit will receive two numbered hang-tag guest passes. Renee Okoro will order the passes and distribute them to units by October 10. Vehicles in guest spaces without a hang-tag after October 10 may be towed after one warning sticker.

7. Open forum
Owners raised noise from the pool pump at night (management to check timer), a request for a second bike rack by Building B (board to get a price), and a question about EV charging (no action; to be revisited in spring).

Action items
- Renee Okoro: sign Carver contract; order guest hang-tags and distribute by October 10; post elevator updates.
- Owen Castellano: request updated reserve study before October 22.
- Priya Nair: circulate new pet registration form to all owners by October 1.
- Linda Marsh: contact Kessler references.

Next meeting: Thursday, October 22, 7 pm, community room.
Adjourned 8:41 pm.

MAPLE COURT APARTMENTS - RESIDENT NOTICE
Issued September 28, 2026 by the Management Office, 410 Alder Street

Dear residents,

This notice covers building work planned for October and November, plus a few reminders about payments and common areas. Please keep it for reference.

1. Water shutoff
The water supply to all units will be shut off on Wednesday, October 14, from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. while the plumbing contractor replaces the main riser valve on the ground floor. Please fill containers the night before if you need water during that window. When service returns, run your cold tap for two to three minutes to clear any discoloured water. If water has not returned by 2:00 p.m., call the office.

2. Elevator modernization
The passenger elevator will be out of service from Monday, October 19 through Friday, November 6 while the cab, controls and doors are replaced. The freight elevator is not available to residents during this period. Residents who need mobility assistance during the elevator work should contact the office by October 9 so we can arrange help with groceries and deliveries. Large deliveries and move-ins will not be scheduled during these three weeks.

3. Parking permits
Annual parking permits expire on October 31. Renewal costs $45 per vehicle and can be completed through the resident portal or at the office. Vehicles without a current permit after November 7 may be towed at the owner's expense. Guest parking is limited to 48 hours per visit; guests must display a paper pass available from the office.

4. Rent payments
Rent is due on the 1st of each month. A late fee of $75 applies if rent has not been received by the end of the 5th. Payments through the resident portal by bank transfer (ACH) have no processing fee. Card payments are accepted but carry a 2.5% processing fee charged by the payment provider. Cash is not accepted at the office.

5. Package room
The package room on the lobby level is open from 7:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. daily. Packages not collected within 10 days will be returned to the carrier. Perishable deliveries should be picked up the same day.

6. Pest inspection
Our pest control vendor will carry out a routine inspection of all kitchens and bathrooms on Tuesday, October 27, between 8:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m. You do not need to be home. Please clear the area under your kitchen sink.

7. Quiet hours and common areas
Quiet hours are 10:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m. The rooftop terrace closes for the season on November 1. The bike storage room is currently full; ask the office to join the waitlist.

8. Lease renewals
Residents whose leases end in the coming months will receive a renewal offer at least 60 days before the lease end date. If you have not received yours by then, please contact the office.

Office hours are Monday to Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. The property manager is Dana Okafor. For after-hours emergencies such as flooding or no heat, call the emergency line listed on the back of your unit door.

Thank you for your patience while we complete these improvements.

Maple Court Management Office

items.question: What if I only plan to keep it three years?
conversation: USER (typed to Natively): I'm trying to decide between leasing a new car and buying a used one. I drive about 8,000 miles a year, I have about 6,000 saved, and I really hate dealing with repairs. Walk me through the trade-offs and tell me which way you'd lean.

NATIVELY: At 8,000 miles a year you're driving well under the average, which is the single biggest factor here. Leasing usually wins on the repair side, since you're covered by warranty for the whole term and you hand the car back before anything major wears out. The catch is that low mileage doesn't lower your payment much, and you're paying for depreciation you'll never own.

Buying used flips that. You own an asset at the end, insurance and registration are typically cheaper, and you're not locked into mileage caps. But you're exposed to repairs once the warranty runs out, which is exactly what you said you hate.

With 6,000 saved, I'd lean toward a used car that's still under its factory warranty, ideally a certified pre-owned one. You get the ownership and lower long-term cost, plus a warranty cushion so repairs aren't your problem for a while. If the monthly payment matters more than owning anything, leasing is the cleaner fit.
items.answer: Three years is short enough that leasing usually wins. You'd be under warranty the whole time, so repairs stay off your plate, and you hand it back before anything major comes due. Buying used only pays off if you keep it longer, since that's when ownership beats the depreciation hit.

items.question: Explain the difference between a credit score and a credit report, who's allowed to see each one, and how long a late payment stays on there.
items.answer:
A credit report is the detailed record: your accounts, balances, payment history, and any collections or bankruptcies. A credit score is a single number calculated from that report, so the report is the source and the score is the summary.

You can see both, and lenders, landlords, and insurers can pull them when you apply. Employers and others need your written permission.

A late payment generally stays on the report for about seven years, though its effect on your score fades as it ages.

items.question: Wait, why do we even have leap years? Is it just every four years, always?
items.answer: Because a year isn't exactly 365 days. Earth takes about 365 and a quarter days to orbit the Sun, so we add a day roughly every four years to keep the calendar lined up with the seasons. items.question: Okay can you explain what an index fund actually is? My dad keeps telling me to buy one and I just nod along.
items.answer: An index fund is a basket that tracks a whole market, like the S&P 500, instead of trying to pick winners. You buy one fund and own a tiny slice of every company in it, so your money rises and falls with the market average. The appeal is low fees and no guesswork, which is why your dad keeps pushing it.
